issues.description: Template StockIngredient defines a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but other template code (Stock.add/take) and the problem statement expect the conventional getter getQuantity(). This method-name mismatch causes compilation errors in the provided template and contradicts the instruction to "add getters for all the private fields." The solution repository uses getQuantity(), showing the intended name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent with the problem statement and the rest of the code: rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() in StockIngredient (or update all callers to use retrieveQuantity). Prefer renaming to getQuantity to follow Java getter conventions and match the solution and Stock usage.

issues.description: The template defines the quantity getter in StockIngredient as retrieveQuantity(), but both the template's Stock class and the solution use/get expect getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields," implying standard getter names. This inconsistent identifier (retrieveQuantity vs getQuantity) breaks the conceptual mapping for the quantity field, causes compilation mismatches in the template (Stock calls getQuantity() which does not exist), and forces students to resolve an unintended naming discrepancy rather than focus on the exercise requirements.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (and keep setQuantity()), so it matches standard getter naming, the usages in Stock.java, and the solution implementation. This aligns with the problem statement's instruction to add getters and removes the accidental mismatch.
